description: In the MPEG-TS demuxer, new_pes_packet() begins transferring ownership of pes->buffer into pkt->buf but only nulls out pes->buffer at the end of the function. The JPEG-XS header-size check added in 16f89d342e returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA mid-function, so on that path both pkt->buf and pes->buffer point to the same refcount-1 buffer. mpegts_read_packet() sees the error, calls av_packet_unref() (freeing the buffer), then its flush loop re-enters new_pes_packet() on the same PES (reset was also skipped so data_index > 0), dereferencing the dangling pes->buffer. A second path reaches the stale pointer via av_buffer_unref() in the seek-reset code in handle_packets, yielding a double-free and an atomic decrement through a freed AVBuffer*. The bug is triggered simply by running ffprobe on a crafted file.
reproduction: 1. Craft an MPEG-TS stream with a PES packet where stream_id==0xbd, stream_type==0x32, bytes 4..7 == 'jxes', and AV_RB32(data) > packet size
2. Deliver the file to the target (e.g. `ffprobe file.ts`)
3. new_pes_packet() takes the early return, leaving pes->buffer == pkt->buf
4. mpegts_read_packet() calls av_packet_unref(), freeing the buffer
5. The flush loop (or later seek-reset in handle_packets) touches the dangling pes->buffer, producing a UAF read or double-free
technical_details:
Hi --

I've filed a PR for a fix that has a similar ffprobe-level failure.

This one is master-only (the vulnerable code landed in 16f89d342e,

December 2025, after 8.0.1 was cut) so there's no released version to

worry about.

It's a use-after-free in the MPEG-TS demuxer's JPEG-XS handling, again

triggers on

  ffprobe arbitrary_file

The specific vulnerability here is that in libavformat/mpegts.c the

function new_pes_packet() moves a buffer from one place to another

(pes into pkt) with the line pkt->buf = pes->buffer. This keeps the

refcount at 1. Then it does JPEG-XS validation, and commits the move

with pes->buffer = NULL at the bottom. But the validation has an early

return that skips the commit:

  // libavformat/mpegts.c, new_pes_packet()

  pkt->buf  = pes->buffer;                           // move started

  pkt->data = pes->buffer->data;

  pkt->size = pes->data_index;

  ...

  if (pes->stream_id == 0xbd && pes->stream_type == 0x32 &&

      pkt->size >= 8 && memcmp(pkt->data + 4, "jxes", 4) == 0)

  {

      uint32_t header_size = AV_RB32(pkt->data);

      if (header_size > pkt->size) {

          ...

          return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;                // move never committed

      }

  }

  ...

  pes->buffer = NULL;                                // not reached

  reset_pes_packet_state(pes);

After the early return, pkt->buf and pes->buffer both hold the same

pointer. But mpegts_read_packet sees the error and calls

av_packet_unref(ts->pkt), freeing the buffer through pkt->buf. Then

its flush loop re-calls new_pes_packet on the same pes -- because

reset_pes_packet_state was also skipped, data_index is still > 0 --

and the dangling pes->buffer gets dereferenced at line 1024.

There's a second path where the dangling pointer survives dormant and

later gets hit by av_buffer_unref(&pes->buffer) in the seek-reset

code at handle_packets.c, which goes to buffer_replace and gives

a double-free plus an atomic-decrement through the stale AVBuffer*.

I tested this against current master:

  [mpegts @ ...] Invalid JPEG-XS header size 4294967295 > packet size 359

  ==2565539==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address

0x509000000808

  READ of size 8 at 0x509000000808 thread T0

      #0 new_pes_packet libavformat/mpegts.c:1024:30

      #1 mpegts_read_packet libavformat/mpegts.c:3495:27

      ...

      #4 avformat_find_stream_info libavformat/demux.c:2800:15

  freed by thread T0 here:

      #3 av_packet_unref libavcodec/packet.c:436:5

      #4 mpegts_read_packet libavformat/mpegts.c:3489:9

I think the fix is pretty clear, which is to do the same cleanup the

success path does before the early return. I've sent this as a PR that

does this:

diff --git a/libavformat/mpegts.c b/libavformat/mpegts.c

index 0ee10f9a77..43b983660f 100644

--- a/libavformat/mpegts.c

+++ b/libavformat/mpegts.c

@@ -1040,7 +1040,8 @@ static int new_pes_packet(PESContext *pes, AVPacket *pkt)

             av_log(pes->stream, AV_LOG_WARNING,

                    "Invalid JPEG-XS header size %"PRIu32" > packet size %d\n",

                    header_size, pkt->size);

-            pes->flags |= AV_PKT_FLAG_CORRUPT;

+            pes->buffer = NULL;

+            reset_pes_packet_state(pes);

             return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;

         }

         pkt->data += header_size;

(The removal for pes->flags is because the call to

reset_pes_packet_state clears the flags.)

Thanks,

Nicholas
title: avformat/mpegts: reset PES state before JPEG-XS error return
